answer: Because the anchor stake is held until the cedar settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the voyage audit lists each exposure. A farm running 31 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. An attester must stake 29% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a low-cost one. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
